substantive_deltas.observation: The repository reports a reduction from 38 to 15 to 0 claim/package schema errors. Four QUALIFIED claims were mapped case-by-case to REFUTED, three SUPPORTED claims to CURRENT, and twelve open-like packet statuses to OPEN while retaining original values and mapping notes.
substantive_deltas.summary_provenance: Seven summaries were produced with mistral-medium-2508 and marked machine-condensed/not human-reviewed. One draft containing source-absent numbers was rejected and regenerated. Two content-thin packets were given descriptive indexes rather than invented findings.
substantive_deltas.epistemic_credit: No independent replication and no new empirical credit. Machine summaries are same-lineage derivations of existing packet content.
substantive_deltas.risk: A green schema can conceal a semantic polarity change if normalization is evaluated only syntactically.

substantive_deltas.observation: PR 232 now separates monotonic elapsed-duration measurement from wall-clock HTTP-date Retry-After arithmetic.
substantive_deltas.epistemic_credit: No live provider validation credit. Zero-step results are retained as null evidence.

primary_sources.title: W3C PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
primary_sources.support: Models provenance using Entity, Activity, and Agent relations, suitable for separating source packets, transformation activity, software agent, and review state.

primary_sources.title: Python 3.13 time.monotonic documentation
primary_sources.support: A monotonic clock cannot go backwards, is unaffected by system clock updates, and is meaningful only through differences.

primary_sources.title: RFC 9110 Retry-After
primary_sources.support: Retry-After is either an HTTP-date or a delay-seconds value, requiring explicit interpretation of the clock domain.

hypotheses.claim: Schema normalization is epistemically safe only when the original value, mapping rule, source hash, transformation activity/agent, validation receipt, and human-review state remain queryable.
hypotheses.test: Reconstruct every pre-repair status and summary provenance from the normalized store; inject polarity-changing mappings and require the semantic-conservation gate to reject them.
hypotheses.falsifier: The normalized store passes reconstruction and polarity checks without retaining one or more of these provenance fields.

hypotheses.claim: A machine-condensed summary contributes navigation value but zero independent epistemic credit unless each proposition is traceable to source spans and its review state is explicit.
hypotheses.test: Run numeric and nonnumeric entity/relation perturbation suites; require source-span entailment and prevent summary nodes from increasing evidence counts.
hypotheses.falsifier: Independent blind assessment shows reliable new empirical information not present in any source packet.

hypotheses.claim: Elapsed duration must use a monotonic clock, while HTTP-date Retry-After needs wall-clock arithmetic anchored to response receipt; mixing them creates false cooldown or duration decisions under clock adjustment.
hypotheses.test: Inject backward/forward wall-clock jumps and compare delay-seconds and HTTP-date paths against a monotonic-duration oracle on an executing provider lane.
hypotheses.falsifier: A single-clock implementation matches the oracle across preregistered jumps, formats, and boundary cases without negative durations or shifted cooldowns.

counterhypotheses.claim: Schema validity alone guarantees semantic safety.
counterhypotheses.counterevidence: A blanket QUALIFIED-to-CURRENT rule would have turned four reported contradictions into held claims; case-level reading instead mapped them to REFUTED.

counterhypotheses.claim: One wall clock is sufficient for both elapsed timing and absolute Retry-After dates.
counterhypotheses.attack: System clock adjustments can alter elapsed deltas even though duration should remain invariant.

new_concepts.name: Semantic Conservation Ledger
new_concepts.definition: A provenance graph that records each normalization transform, original semantic token, polarity, source hash, transformer, validator, and review state so schema repair remains reversible and auditable.

new_concepts.name: Schema-Green Mirage
new_concepts.definition: A syntactically valid corpus whose semantic polarity, evidence independence, or review status was silently changed during normalization.

new_concepts.name: Derived Summary Quarantine
new_concepts.definition: A graph policy that permits machine summaries for retrieval but blocks them from increasing evidence counts or promotion confidence until source-span and review gates pass.

new_concepts.name: Dual-Clock Receipt
new_concepts.definition: An execution receipt that records monotonic start/end deltas separately from wall-clock response time and absolute Retry-After interpretation.

routing.impulse: Implement or test the Semantic Conservation Ledger and Derived Summary Quarantine; do not count normalized or machine-derived summaries as independent evidence.
